title: Meeting Stan Kenton
summary: Kenton and Pete Rugolo come to the Palladium and borrow the rhythm section to record Machito.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: How did you start getting involved with the various jazz people? Now, Gillespie was -- Dizzy was playing around -- Dizzy sat in with you, you said.
Can you get into a bit, both the relationship with Kenton and the relationship with --

Well, the relationship with Kenton was very (inaudible). Kenton came -- the first appearance in the Paramount Theater. He heard about this Machito orchestra. So he came to the Palladium with Pete Rugolo (inaudible) and a couple of guys, (inaudible) to listen to the band. So first time he (inaudible) and left. So then every night when we're closing to the theater (inaudible) the Palladium (inaudible).

So he said, well, Mario, I want a recording (inaudible). I want you to help me. So, all right. (Inaudible). He said, how about you lending me your rhythm section to record. Sure, I'll be glad to. So we took a whole rhythm section to the Parfait (phonetic) Studio, 106th between Park Avenue and (inaudible). Machito went too, you know, combine everything, made a record. And then in (inaudible) to that he had Pete Rugolo wrote a tune called (inaudible) Machito. That was how -- how we got acquainted.
